topIssues.title: op-supernode: Reset Handling
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
# Context

Supernode exists to drive complex or extended protocols through derivation and verification. For example, Supernode's Interop Activity confirms that the chains being derived all contain valid Executing Messages.

Because Verification occurs based on chain state, it is *REQUIRED* that the EVM underneath the Supernode sometimes arrive at chain states which are invalid. Invalid Executing Messages must exist to be deemed invalid.

AND YET! The Supernode must allow follow the canonical chain in order to *continue* verifying blocks.

Fundamentally, this means we need the ability to *rewind*, *truncate*, *reorg* or *reset* the Chain State which the Supernode uses.

# Reset Requirements

Resets should follow timestamp as their primary indexing, and should be chain specific.

`Supernode.Reset(ChainID, Timestamp)`

Likely, this functionality only needs to be fully exposed at the Chain Container Level, for production/interop purposes

`ChainContainer.Reset(Timestamp)`

When Resetting, the Chain Container is responsible for fully restoring the chain state to the expected timestamp. This means it should:
- Suspend the ongoing Virutal Node
- Reset the Executing Engine to truncate data beyond the timestamp
- Resume the ongoing Virtual Node

This is the strategy employed in the SV2 spike, logic flow available here: https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Supervisor-V2-Main-Loop-and-Logic-Flow-Diagrams-265f153ee162804388dac933f525de7b

# Considerations
- In the POC, we had to use `DebugSetHead`. Hopefully we can find a cleaner way to handle it
- It might be prudent to manually truncate the SafeDB while the CL is being replaced since we have a handle to it, but the CL should also handle that.

# Tools at your disposal
- The Chain Container loop already is pretty graceful about replacing the Virtual Node. A new VN is created with a new `vn_id` and all prior resources are hooked to it.
- Engine Controller as an entity can house all the complexity for resetting the EL. The Chain Container keeps a persistent handle over the EVM across all VNs so it can do work like this and also read state.

# How it connects to other work
- When Interop Activity discovers a bad block it's going to tell the Chain Container via a `InvalidateBlock` function
- Invalidate block will cause the Chain Container to store the ID in the "Denylist" registry, which prevents re-derivation to invalid blocks
- The chain container will *then also* notice the EVM is on that invalid state, and will trigger a reset

# How you can test this work
- Gotta get Acceptance Testing built out more, but there's already a preset for the Supernode we can build from
- You could easily build a reset API by implementing an `RPCActivity` that triggers the functionality. That way you could run the supernode locally and poke the feature. You wouldn't need to commit the activity since there's no production reason to reset nodes (though... maybe that's the start of an admin API)

# Definition of Done

- A Chain can be reset back to a timestamp
- Without further integration to Verification Activities, the same chain-state is expected to re-derive
- We should be able to see this live through some demo
- Unit tests from the Chain Container that the correct calls to the CL+EL are being done and VN is replaced
- Integration (Acceptance) test that demonstrates reset and re-derivation

topIssues.title: op-reth: batcher throttling
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Background on batcher-sequencer throttling in our docs: https://docs.optimism.io/chain-operators/guides/configuration/batcher#batcher-sequencer-throttling

op-geth provides an endpoint `miner_setMaxDASize` to allow the batcher to throttle individual tx and full block size, as estimated by transaction DA usage. op-reth and op-rbuilder implement this endpoint already, but as a stub. It doesn't do anything.

The implementation inside op-geth can be followed at [`miner/worker.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/733bb5b623f7e9682771764f3eb402292da892f4/miner/worker.go?plain=1#L498 ), `Miner.commitTransactions`. Follow the use of `blockDABytes` for the block DA limit and how `MaxDATxSize` is used in the `txpool.PendingFilter`, set at [`Miner.fillTransactions`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/733bb5b623f7e9682771764f3eb402292da892f4/miner/worker.go?plain=1#L696).

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Safe Label Adjusting
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
# Context

There are multiple levels of understanding over the chain

EL <- the actual state of the machine

CL <- the state of local derivation

Super <- the _verified_ superchain state


Customers today query the EL's `Safe` label and expect it to mean something: this data won't revert (unless the L1 reverts).

However, this convention breaks with extended protocol features, because the CL will drive the EL and call the Locally Derived Content "Safe"

And we _also_ need for the "Locally Derived" head to be known for the batcher 

See: https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Supernode-API-Decision-What-is-Safe-2cef153ee16280c19dffcde8ca930957?showMoveTo=true&saveParent=true

# Task

This task has the open product/design question of what we want to support. We can limit scope to the CL or EL selectively to make solving this problem easier. But where appropriate, we need to make sure the distinction between "published" and "verified" definitions of Safe are distincted for clients who need it.

topIssues.title: challenger: Introduce supernode provider
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body: Integrate a supernode provider to eventually replace the supervisor provider. Since the supernode API isn't fully implemented yet, the challenger should continue using the supervisor provider to maintain e2e testing coverage. Ideally, we can hide both API variants behind a unified interface to make the eventual migration to supernode seamless. I suggest refactoring the `super.RootProvider` interface and the `SuperTraceProvider` to accommodate both APIs.

topIssues.title: contracts: Add rootClaim(uint256 l2ChainId) to IDisputeGame
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
In preparation for interop, let's extend the IDisputeGame interface to support the `rootClaim(uint256 l2ChainId) returns (Claim)` method.

This new method will allow users to retrieve the Claim for a particular L2 chain ID. For pre-interop dispute games, this simply returns the root claim.
But for the `SuperDisputeGame.sol`, this should return the claimed output root of the given L2 chain ID. For now, the `SuperDisputeGame.sol` implementation should revert until it can be created with a super root preimage.
